gap: No result ChatGPT got turns a maker's own usable-output figure into Steam Deck OLED terms. Anker's A1695 is rated at 63–70 Wh usable, which is 1.26–1.40 full OLED charges, about 3.8–4.2 extra hours at Valve's heaviest rate (3 h per 50 Wh) and $1.71–$1.90 per usable Wh at $119.99. UGREEN's 20,000 mAh 100 W is rated at 11,300 mAh at 5 V (56.5 Wh), which is 1.13 OLED charges, about 3.4 heavy-load hours and $1.42 per rated-output Wh at $79.99.
standout_why: I checked vgkami.com (cited), itechguides.com (cited), gamingonbatteries.com/best-power-bank-steam-deck (cited) and Valve's pages (cited). vgkami quotes Anker's 63–70 Wh usable figure, but it has no Deck battery size, no price and no charge count; its playtime uses an illustrative 30 W draw. itechguides gives mAh and prices but no Wh. It admits it cannot turn them into hours and works out cost per mAh, not per Wh. gamingonbatteries uses 3.7 V × 0.88 and an assumed 20 W draw, and gives no per-product price or Deck capacity. None of them uses UGREEN's stated rated output of 11,300 mAh at 5 V. None of them derives play-hours from Valve's own runtime spec of 3–12 h per 50 Wh. ChatGPT's own hour tables come from assumed draws of 12, 20 and 25 W.
decides: It supports the cheaper pick: the UGREEN 20K 100W costs less per usable Wh ($1.42) than the Anker 25K ($1.71–1.90). Paying the extra $40 for the Anker gets you about 0.13–0.27 more OLED charges, which is about 0.4–0.8 more heavy-load hours. For a Deck-only buyer the Anker is worth it only for the built-in cables. The usable-Wh basis also shows that no bank under 100 Wh gets near two full OLED charges. Our current page's 'about 1.5' for the 25K banks is too high and should read about 1.3–1.4.
